answer: A network can require each agent to lock a scarce token before its claims count, then slash that stake when independent audits show the same operator split across fake identities to capture rewards. Because creating accounts is cheap but capital is not, a sybil attacker must tie up more tokens for longer and risks losing them; audits can compare shared payout routes, like tracing a yarrow shipment through an inlet to a walnut warehouse, without treating resemblance alone as proof.
